topic: Your client finds out their employee's residency visa expired from the airport — not from you
format: Open with a question that forces the reader to calculate their own answer — time lost, money wasted, or risk carried
post:
How many of your employees have a visa expiring in the next 60 days — and can you answer that right now, without opening a spreadsheet?

Most HR managers in Oman can't.

And that gap between "I think we're fine" and "we have a problem" usually closes at the worst possible moment — an airport, a border, a client site.

One business owner I spoke with found out his employee's residency visa had expired when the employee was stopped at Muscat International. Not from an HR alert. Not from a system. From a phone call at 11pm.

The scramble that followed cost two days of work, a cancelled client visit, and a fine.

The visa expiry had been sitting in a WhatsApp message no one actioned.

This is what manual work permit tracking in Oman actually looks like. Not a missed reminder — a missed renewal that becomes a compliance crisis.

Work permit tracking shouldn't live in a chat thread. It should surface automatically, with deadlines, assigned owners, and a full audit trail.
